luke.24.p1.b1.text: On the first day of the week, very early in the morning, the women came to the tomb, bringing the spices they had prepared.

luke.24.p1.b2.text: They found the stone rolled away from the tomb,

luke.24.p1.b3.text: but when they entered, they did not find the body of the Lord Jesus.

luke.24.p2.b1.text: While they were puzzling over this, suddenly two men in radiant apparel stood beside them.

luke.24.p2.b2.text: “Why do you look for the living among the dead?

luke.24.p2.b3.text: He is not here; He has risen!

luke.24.p2.b4.text: ‘The Son of Man must be delivered into the hands of sinful men, and be crucified, and on the third day rise again.’

luke.24.p3.b2.text: It was Mary Magdalene, Joanna, Mary the mother of James, and the other women with them who told this to the apostles.

luke.24.p3.b3.text: But their words seemed like nonsense to them, and they did not believe the women.

luke.24.p4.b1.text: Peter, however, got up and ran to the tomb.

luke.24.p4.b2.text: And after bending down and seeing only the linen cloths,

luke.24.p4.b3.text: he went away, wondering to himself what had happened.

luke.24.p5.b1.text: That same day two of them were going to a village called Emmaus,

luke.24.p5.b2.text: They were talking with each other about everything that had happened.

luke.24.p5.b3.text: Jesus Himself came up and walked along with them.

luke.24.p5.b4.text: But their eyes were kept from recognizing Him.

luke.24.p6.b1.text: “What are you discussing so intently as you walk along?”

luke.24.p6.b2.text: They stood still, with sadness on their faces.

luke.24.p6.b3.text: One of them, named Cleopas, asked Him,

luke.24.p6.b4.text: “Are You the only visitor to Jerusalem who does not know the things that have happened there in recent days?”

luke.24.p7.b2.text: “The events involving Jesus of Nazareth,” … “This man was a prophet, powerful in speech and action before God and all the people.

luke.24.p7.b3.text: Our chief priests and rulers delivered Him up to the sentence of death, and they crucified Him.

luke.24.p7.b4.text: But we were hoping He was the One who would redeem Israel.

luke.24.p8.b1.text: Furthermore, some of our women astounded us. They were at the tomb early this morning,

luke.24.p8.b2.text: They came and told us they had seen a vision of angels, who said that Jesus was alive.

luke.24.p8.b3.text: Then some of our companions went to the tomb and found it just as the women had described.

luke.24.p8.b4.text: But Him they did not see.”

luke.24.p9.b1.text: “O foolish ones, how slow are your hearts to believe all that the prophets have spoken!

luke.24.p9.b2.text: Was it not necessary for the Christ to suffer these things and then to enter His glory?”

luke.24.p9.b3.text: And beginning with Moses and all the Prophets, He explained to them what was written in all the Scriptures about Himself.

luke.24.p10.b1.text: As they approached the village where they were headed, He seemed to be going farther.

luke.24.p10.b2.text: “Stay with us, for it is nearly evening and the day is almost over.”

luke.24.p10.b3.text: So He went in to stay with them.

luke.24.p11.b1.text: While He was reclining at the table with them, He took bread, spoke a blessing

luke.24.p11.b2.text: and broke it, and gave it to them.

luke.24.p11.b3.text: Then their eyes were opened and they recognized Jesus

luke.24.p11.b4.text: and He disappeared from their sight.

luke.24.p12.b1.text: “Were not our hearts burning within us as He spoke with us on the road and opened the Scriptures to us?”

luke.24.p12.b2.text: And they got up that very hour and returned to Jerusalem.

luke.24.p12.b3.text: “The Lord has indeed risen and has appeared to Simon!”

luke.24.p12.b4.text: Then the two told what had happened on the road, and how they had recognized Jesus in the breaking of the bread.

luke.24.p13.b1.text: While they were describing these events,

luke.24.p13.b3.text: But they were startled and frightened, thinking they had seen a spirit.

luke.24.p13.b4.text: Look at My hands and My feet. It is I Myself. Touch Me and see

luke.24.p14.b1.text: While they were still in disbelief because of their joy and amazement,

luke.24.p14.b2.text: “Do you have anything here to eat?”

luke.24.p14.b3.text: So they gave Him a piece of broiled fish,

luke.24.p14.b4.text: and He took it and ate it in front of them.

luke.24.p15.b1.text: Everything must be fulfilled that is written about Me in the Law of Moses, the Prophets, and the Psalms.”

luke.24.p15.b2.text: Then He opened their minds to understand the Scriptures.

luke.24.p15.b3.text: This is what is written: The Christ will suffer and rise from the dead on the third day,

luke.24.p15.b4.text: and in His name repentance and forgiveness of sins will be proclaimed to all nations, beginning in Jerusalem.

luke.24.p16.b1.text: You are witnesses of these things.

luke.24.p16.b2.text: And behold, I am sending the promise of My Father upon you.

luke.24.p16.b3.text: But remain in the city until you have been clothed with power from on high.”

luke.24.p17.b1.text: When Jesus had led them out as far as Bethany,

luke.24.p17.b2.text: He lifted up His hands and blessed them.

luke.24.p17.b3.text: While He was blessing them, He left them and was carried up into heaven.

luke.24.p19.b1.text: praising God continually in the temple.
